title: How can the shell make room?
hook: A rigid covering poses a growth problem.

knows: A hard outer covering can support an animal.
doesNotKnow: Explain a simple role of molting in arthropod growth.

misconception: An arthropod can grow indefinitely without replacing a restrictive cuticle.
objective: Explain a simple role of molting in arthropod growth.

claims.text: A rigid covering poses a growth problem. As an arthropod grows, what can make room for a larger body when its outer cuticle is restrictive? The example shows an animal leaving its old outer cuticle and expanding a new one before it hardens. Many arthropods grow through repeated molts; the precise timing and growth pattern differ among species.

claims.text: The stage uses a simplified, not-to-scale schematic and stated model assumptions; it is not a photographic observation of an individual animal.
Recall: A growing arthropod leaves an old outer covering behind. What is this process called? Molting is the shedding of the old cuticle.
